html:
Install and startup

Start from source

This guide installs SMTO from source code, meaning the original project files rather than a ready-made installer. You need Python 3.11 or newer, a copy of the project supplied by the maintainer, and an AI model that works with SMTO. These steps use a terminal, an app for entering commands. You may need help from someone with technical experience.

For ready-made downloads, visit the release repository and choose the folder for your operating system. Follow the instructions supplied with those files; the commands below apply to a source checkout. For compiled dependency setup, status and repair, use the compiled installation instructions. The dependency flow guide explains what happens internally and how interrupted setup resumes.

SMTO has a main program that manages tasks and a Gateway program that runs tools on the computer you choose. The AI model runs in an engine process or online service. On Linux, the controller can manage vLLM and llama.cpp through Inference. Read the installer before running it, and use a computer you are allowed to manage.

The installer displays the License and EULA before it changes anything. It asks you to accept the License, then to accept the EULA and proceed with installation. Type y or yes at each prompt; uppercase answers also work. Pressing Enter without an answer or entering anything else cancels. Read them without installing with ./install.sh --show-license and ./install.sh --show-eula. Windows PowerShell uses -ShowLicense and -ShowEula on its Gateway installer.

For unattended setup, supply both --accept-license VERSION and --accept-eula VERSION using the versions displayed by that installer. PowerShell uses -AcceptLicense VERSION and -AcceptEula VERSION. --non-interactive (-NonInteractive in PowerShell) disables prompting but does not accept the terms. Piped answers and --yes cannot accept them. Each install, upgrade or repair requires acceptance; the main installer shares it with its local Gateway setup only during that invocation. Installer acceptance is separate from the product's first-use EULA acceptance.

On Linux and macOS, installation shows the current step, a spinner with elapsed time, and a completion or failure message. Redirected output uses plain status lines. Password prompts remain visible and pause progress animation. Add --verbose for full command output, for example ./install.sh --verbose. The Windows PowerShell installer uses -Verbose.

Source installers compile the prompt catalog before installing runtime packages. You do not need to run the prompt compiler separately after updating the source. If compilation fails, installation stops before changing runtime packages; inspect the reported log, correct the prompt sources, and rerun the installer. Wheel, source-archive and compiled binary builds generate and validate the catalog in their staging directories without changing the checkout.

Install on Linux

Open a terminal in the project folder. Run the installer:

./install.sh

Start the Gateway, which runs tools on this computer:

./src/gateway_agent/startup.sh

In another terminal in the project folder, start the main SMTO program:

./startup.sh

Each Gateway start prints Gateway connection details: its host/IP, port, HTTPS URL, node name, and public key fingerprint. Copy these fields into Settings > Gateways > Add Gateway on the server and choose a nickname. The output identifies local-only listeners and explains how to enable connections from another computer. Outbound Gateways show their server destination and node instead, since they do not open an inbound listener.

Each server start prints Server connection details, including browser URLs with the active HTTP or HTTPS scheme and port. For wildcard listeners, the output lists local interface addresses as well as a URL for the same computer. These sections also appear in redirected startup logs and on subsequent restarts.

Linux source installation includes inference management automatically; no extra enable flag is needed. Use ./install.sh --launch to install and immediately start the controller instead. Open Inference at /inference to configure a runtime, model and instance, then explicitly launch it. Installation does not download or launch a model, or adopt an existing standalone portal.

For compiled Linux x86_64 installations, select smto-server-inference for integrated management or smto-server-external for external endpoints. The compiled builder's --inference=both|enabled|disabled selects the artifacts; Linux server builds default to both. That option belongs to ./build/build, not install.sh. A runtime setting cannot add inference to an external-only binary. See Inference management for the complete setup workflow.

Install on macOS

Use the same installer and main startup command. For the Gateway, use ./src/gateway_macos/startup.sh instead of the Linux command.

To use a Mac only as a computer that runs tools, use ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh and ./src/gateway_macos/startup.sh. This installs the Gateway and its required software without installing the main SMTO program. It also attempts to set up optional tools such as Browser.

Use a Windows computer to run tools

The Windows Gateway uses src/gateway_windows/install.ps1 and src/gateway_windows/startup.ps1 in PowerShell. These set up the computer that runs tools; they are not instructions for installing the main SMTO program on Windows.

Set up portal sign-in

The Server installer asks you to create a local owner account and preserves an existing valid account. Follow Portal owner sign-in below for private password-file input, local setup/reset commands and password changes. Gateway-only installation uses its separate pairing workflow.

Enable HTTPS and browser trust

Open Settings → HTTPS & Certificates and enter the hostnames and IP addresses used to reach this server. Choose Install trusted root certificate to prepare its persistent root CA before switching to HTTPS. Preparation does not restart anything. Compare the displayed SHA-256 fingerprint before trusting the root.

Under Generate a local HTTPS certificate, use IPv4 range → Add range to fill the IP address list. For example, 192.168.1.x adds every address from 192.168.1.0 through 192.168.1.255, including .0 and .255. Trailing X or * also works, and you can use any IPv4 prefix. Existing entries are preserved and duplicates removed. The list supports up to 1,024 IP addresses. Broader patterns such as 192.168.x.x contain 65,536 addresses and must be narrowed. Certificates require individual IP addresses, so the helper expands the pattern before submission. Adding a range only edits the form; choose Generate & Apply when ready to save the certificate and restart web services.

On a local desktop server, Install on this computer installs system-wide trust using the operating system's administrator prompt. For a remote server, container, WSL instance, or system service, download the bundle for the device running your browser. Open that bundle on the browser's device and follow its instructions; smTO and Python are not needed there. A download is not an installed certificate.

Windows and macOS use their system certificate stores. Linux uses its distribution's trust tools and also imports the certificate into the invoking user's Chromium and Firefox databases. Read each installation result: a locked browser profile or missing NSS utility can require closing the browser, installing the named utility, or importing the public root through the browser's certificate settings. New profiles and other users may need a separate import. Restart browsers after installing trust.

On Android, download the root and import it as a CA certificate in the device's security settings. On iOS/iPadOS, install the downloaded profile in General → VPN & Device Management, then enable Full Trust in General → About → Certificate Trust Settings. Managed devices may restrict these actions.

After installing trust, choose Apply trusted certificate & restart. The server saves active work and restarts the application, console, and bundled manual using HTTPS. Existing application-generated self-signed certificates are reissued under the root while preserving their hostnames and compatible key. Uploaded certificates remain unchanged by trust setup. New certificates default to 365 days, with a maximum of 825; migration previews 365 days for an older certificate configured above that limit. The root lasts ten years and survives certificate regeneration and upgrades.

Root trust fixes an unknown issuer only for certificates signed by that root. The address in your browser must also match a DNS name or IP address on the certificate, and the certificate must be valid. Settings identifies address mismatches. Installing trust never disables certificate verification, changes the active protocol, or restarts web services. Cancelled authorization or partial installation can be retried.

Open SMTO and connect your AI

After the main program starts, open its /agent-ui page in a browser. With the default setup on the same computer, the address is http://127.0.0.1:8011/agent-ui. While saved data loads, an initialization page shows the current stage and elapsed time. It opens the requested page automatically when the program is ready.

If startup fails, the page says SMTO couldn't start and explains in plain words what went wrong and how to fix it. Technical details shows the exact error, with passwords, tokens and keys removed, and Copy error details copies it for whoever helps you. When SMTO recognizes a problem it can repair safely, a SMTO can fix this for you box offers Auto Fix. For example, it can stop another copy of SMTO that is using the same data (that copy saves its work first), or give your account back access to a data folder it owns. After you fix a cause yourself, select Start again. Only an admin account can use Auto Fix and Start again. Refreshing the page does not retry startup.

Requesting /restart switches the workspace to the same progress screen for shutdown. A flashing red indicator shows that shutdown is underway; normal workspace controls remain unavailable. Expand the phases to see service stops, pending operations, repository saves, validation, durable publication, and elapsed timings. Remaining-time estimates use measured progress or previous shutdowns when available. The screen then shows startup and returns to your original page when the new process is ready. If the final save fails, the screen explains the failure and offers Retry restart while keeping the workspace locked.

/shutdown stops the server and every enabled Gateway; /shutdownserver stops only the server and leaves Gateways running. Both are administrator commands. The same progress screen shows the final save, then Server stopped once the save is confirmed and the server, manual and troubleshooting console have exited. Nothing restarts on its own: start SMTO again on the host (installed services stay stopped until started). The open page checks periodically and returns to the workspace when the server is back. If the final save fails, the server keeps running with its data in memory and the screen offers Retry shutdown. A Gateway that is running a Gateway-managed LLM refuses to shut down; stop the model first.

In Mission Control, choose the Gateway and configure your model connection. With integrated inference, launch an instance and select Use this connection in Inference → Overview. For external models, enter the connection details in Model Configuration. Select the model before asking the assistant to do work.

The main program uses port 8011 and the Gateway uses 8787 by default. A port is the number in a network address that identifies a service. The startup script also opens the manual on port 8013 and a troubleshooting console on port 8015. They close when the main startup script exits. The Gateway and external AI services have their own start and stop commands. Managed inference instances use the Inference controls; inference subsystem restart/shutdown keeps the controller UI available.

For a direct Uvicorn launch from the project folder, use:

.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn --app-dir src smto_runtime.server:create_app --factory --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8011 --timeout-graceful-shutdown 5

Service monitors can use /livez to check that the web server is responding and /healthz to check runtime readiness. /healthz and runtime APIs return HTTP 503 during initialization or after initialization failure; /api/startup reports the stage and status without reading the database. Detailed startup diagnostics require portal sign-in. Anonymous health probes receive only the availability result and its HTTP status, rather than startup errors or runtime identifiers. The eager agent_runtime.api.app:create_app factory remains available for embedded callers.

While saved data loads, the browser shows Preparing your workspace, the current startup step, and elapsed time. The page uses the app’s shared theme and cube mark; it follows your tab’s light/dark override, or your device theme until saved settings are available. The progress animation respects reduced-motion preferences. Leave the page open: it reconnects automatically and opens your original page, including any conversation link, when startup finishes. If startup fails, it shows the failed step and recovery instructions instead of continuing the loading animation.

Expand the report to inspect measured phases and work counts. An unknown total or missing remaining-time estimate is left unknown; it does not mean progress has stopped. /diagnostics/startup retains this process's startup report after it is ready. See Server lifecycle ownership for the implementation boundaries, history limits and shutdown guarantees.

For advanced setup, AOR_MANUAL_AUTOSTART=0 and AOR_CONSOLE_AUTOSTART=0 turn off those automatic starts. ./startmanual.sh starts the manual separately. Do not start a second copy on a port already in use. Availability of ready-made downloads is listed separately on the website's Download page.

Gateway pairing and platform setup

For connection recovery, stop the Gateway and its automatic restart service, then run the command for your installation:

Installation Reset command
Compiled Gateway ./smto-gateway-linux-x86_64 reset (use your platform's executable)
Linux source ./src/gateway_agent/reset.sh or ./src/gateway_agent/startup.sh reset
macOS source ./src/gateway_macos/reset.sh or ./src/gateway_macos/startup.sh reset
Windows source ./src/gateway_windows/reset.ps1
Installed Python environment python -m gateway_core.reset

Use the same OS account and GATEWAY_TLS_STATE_DIR as startup. Add --dry-run to preview without changing files, or --tls-state-dir PATH to select an explicit state directory. The PowerShell equivalents are -DryRun and -TlsStateDir PATH. Reset clears controller pairing, saved outbound server identity pins, and abandoned authentication temporary files. It preserves the Gateway's TLS identity, replay protection, job history, artifacts, downloaded files, and configuration. It does not stop jobs or repair installed dependencies. Restart the Gateway and connect the intended controller. A runtime lease blocks reset while a current Gateway is using that state; older Gateway versions must be stopped explicitly.

To reset Gateway controller pairing, stop the Gateway and run ./src/gateway_agent/reset-pairing.sh on Linux or ./src/gateway_macos/reset-pairing.sh on macOS. Use the same OS account and GATEWAY_TLS_STATE_DIR setting as startup. Then restart the Gateway and connect the intended controller. These scripts use the Gateway's installed virtual environment and preserve its TLS identity.

macOS requires a 64-bit Python 3.11+ and compatible canonical dependencies. Existing PATH, MacPorts, Homebrew, and Python.org framework interpreters are discovered even when standard install locations are absent from PATH. Use PYTHON_BIN=/path/to/python3.11 to select a specific interpreter. With no compatible Python, the installer can use an existing package manager: AOR_MACOS_PACKAGE_MANAGER=auto prefers Homebrew on Apple Silicon and MacPorts on Intel, then tries the other usable manager. homebrew and macports force one manager; none prevents package installation. AOR_SKIP_SYSTEM_DEPS=1, GATEWAY_SKIP_SYSTEM_DEPS=1 (Gateway only), or AOR_INSTALL_SYSTEM_DEPS=0 also prevent installation. Root setup passes its resolved Python to Gateway setup with GATEWAY_SKIP_SYSTEM_DEPS=1 to avoid duplicate system installs.

Neither package manager is bootstrapped, and shell profiles and global Python selection are left alone. Existing Python can run the core Gateway without either manager; missing Git only disables Git-specific workflows. Intel and Apple Silicon installer support does not certify every older macOS version. Optional browser components can impose stricter requirements; their failure leaves Browser unavailable without blocking core installation. Both root and standalone installers record optional failures in each venv's smto-installation.json. Repair dependencies, rerun installation and restart services to retry those features. See the macOS Gateway guide for examples and diagnostics.

Configure the model endpoint with the active LLM settings and use the inference defaults in src/agent_runtime/llm/product_profile.py. Provider/model processes are separate from the deterministic runtime. See src/llm/README.md for model launch scripts.

./setupplaywright.sh installs Chromium for UI tests. It creates no runtime browser profile.

Set AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR for an isolated state directory. Preserve existing user databases when upgrading. Seed builders are for fresh development installations, not resetting a running user's data.

A source checkout keeps its Server data (accounts, chats, settings and saved state) in ./artifacts, and its controller identity in ~/.smto/controller/identity. An installed Server instance keeps both in one folder, ~/.local/share/smto/data/server/INSTANCE, with state/, identity/ and tls/ inside. To run the source checkout on an installed instance's data, pass that folder:

./startup.sh --data-dir ~/.local/share/smto/data/server/inference

--data-dir also accepts the instance's state/ folder, or any other state folder such as ./artifacts. It refuses a folder that does not exist rather than creating an empty one. Only one Server can own a data folder at a time, so stop the installed instance first. Both should run the same release: an older build may not read state saved by a newer one.

Public manual

The public website uses https://smtorch.com. Its manual is served separately at https://manual.smtorch.com/manual; the service root redirects to /manual.

Prepare the repository environment with ./setup-manual.sh, then run:

./scripts/start-smto-manual.sh

On Windows, install the project with its manual extra into .venv, then use ./scripts/start-smto-manual.ps1. Both launchers accept --host, --port, and --reload. CLI options override AOR_MANUAL_HOST, AOR_MANUAL_PORT, and AOR_MANUAL_RELOAD. The defaults are 127.0.0.1:8013 with reload disabled. SMTO_MANUAL_PYTHON selects a different interpreter. The launchers check dependencies and start one manual process; they do not install packages or start the Agent, Gateway, or website. The public manual always uses product branding and does not query personal Agent settings. ./startmanual.sh retains local sidecar behavior through --local.

For a Linux deployment, place the checkout and its .venv at /opt/smto-manual and run the service as a dedicated smto-manual user. Adapt packaging/manual/smto-manual.service.example to your installation. It gives generated manual references a writable cache under /var/cache/smto-manual while keeping the checkout read-only. Use packaging/manual/Caddyfile.example to terminate HTTPS and proxy manual.smtorch.com to 127.0.0.1:8013. Point the subdomain's DNS to that host and make its HTTPS endpoint reachable before activating the proxy.

Only one process can own port 8013. When the public launcher and the Agent run on the same host, set AOR_MANUAL_AUTOSTART=0 for the Agent. Stopping the public launcher stops only its own manual process; an occupied port is an error, not a request to stop another service. Keep reload disabled in the deployed service.

App manual links retain their local behavior: localhost and private LAN hosts use the app host on the configured manual port (8013 by default). Public app hosts link to https://manual.smtorch.com/manual, preserving document and heading fragments.

Account sign-in and user administration

Every Server installation starts with one administrator account. After accepting the installation terms, choose a username and an 8–128-character password, then confirm the hidden password. Upgrades from installations without login require this step; subsequent updates keep the existing account. Gateway-only installation does not ask for it.

Open the main Server interface and sign in. Each account receives a private workspace. Administrators open Settings → Users (/user) to manage users and can access the diagnostic console. Sign out using the interface; sessions expire after 12 hours without automatic renewal. Use ./startup.sh --https for network access, or configure a trusted HTTPS reverse proxy. The console follows the Server's HTTP/HTTPS mode.

For an installation without saved certificate settings, the compatibility environment options select an existing certificate and its matching private key:

AOR_SSL_CERTFILE=/etc/smto/server.crt AOR_SSL_KEYFILE=/etc/smto/server.key ./startup.sh --https

Use a certificate trusted by your browsers and CLI clients and valid for the Server's hostname. Saved HTTPS & Certificates configuration takes precedence over these environment options. If neither legacy certificate file exists, HTTPS startup can generate a certificate signed by the installation's local root. HTTP remains available for local development; HTTPS enables secure cookies. When terminating TLS at a reverse proxy, restrict direct backend access and forward the original HTTPS scheme only through a proxy trusted by the ASGI server.

For unattended installation, add --portal-username OWNER --portal-password-file FILE to the existing versioned License/EULA acceptance options. Supply a private UTF-8 file (mode 0600 on Linux/macOS, owner/SYSTEM access on Windows). A final line ending is ignored; other spaces and Unicode are preserved. No plaintext password option exists.

To change your password, open Settings → Account (/account), enter your current password, then enter and confirm a new 8–128-character password. Spaces and Unicode are preserved. Select Change password to save. Your current browser stays signed in; every other session is signed out.

To recover locally, run .venv/bin/aor auth reset under the Server's OS account and state-directory environment. Keep the same working directory when the state path is relative; --state-dir PATH explicitly selects the state root. With multiple accounts, specify --portal-username USERNAME. Recovery changes only the named account and signs out that account's sessions; it never replaces other accounts. Use aor auth setup to configure a missing account without reinstalling. Both commands support --state-dir, --portal-username, --portal-password-file, and --non-interactive. Packaged Servers expose auth setup and auth reset on their launcher; managed packages also accept --instance NAME.

Credential hashes and session hashes live in the private .auth directory under AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR (default artifacts). Environment rebuilds and normal updates preserve them. Keep that directory private in full installation backups. Workspace JSON backup/import and database relocation do not replace account credentials or roles. Missing or invalid credentials never enable anonymous workspace access. This state is separate from provider OAuth credentials, Gateway pairing and legal acceptance; auth setup/reset does not accept terms or erase conversations.

From Settings → Users (/user), administrators can search, create and edit accounts; assign gateways; set user configuration overrides; reset passwords; revoke sessions; disable or re-enable accounts; and open a selected user's workspace. Temporary passwords require replacement at first sign-in. New normal accounts start empty with no gateway access. Normal users can change personal appearance and task choices within administrator limits. They cannot configure installation models, tools, policies, enrollment, updates or diagnostics.

Opening another account uses /admin/workspaces/USER_ID/…, with an identity banner and a return link. This does not switch the signed-in administrator or another tab. Work launched there belongs to the selected user and obeys that user's access policy.

Disabling cancels active work and pauses schedules and monitors. Remote cancellation that cannot be confirmed is reported as pending. Re-enabling permits sign-in but does not resume work automatically. Delete a disabled account using the separate confirmation; deletion remains pending while gateway cleanup is unconfirmed and resumes after restart. Only managed workspace resources are removed, never arbitrary files on shared machines.

Upgrade preserves the original workspace paths, migrates the existing owner to admin, and revokes old sessions once. New accounts use users/USER_ID/ beneath the state root. The installation/accounts-migration.json journal and verified installation/pre-multiuser-workspace backup support interrupted migration recovery. Keep a full pre-upgrade installation backup, including external configured data paths, authentication and gateway identities. Rollback restores that backup; do not run older binaries against migrated state. Backup copies retain historical data until retired by the operator. Offline workspace backup/import uses --user USERNAME for multiple accounts.

Upgrade gateways before assigning them to additional accounts: they must advertise user_scope_v1. The migrated administrator retains old-gateway compatibility during upgrade. Application records and managed sessions are isolated; shared gateway machine files and processes remain governed by the gateway's OS permissions.

CLI run, chat, and remote doctor also require sign-in, using secure terminal prompts or --portal-username and --portal-password-file. HTTPS certificate verification remains enabled. Gateway connections retain their existing pairing.
